newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH SHARES WEAKEN WITH EYES ON U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH SHARES WEAKEN WITH EYES ON U.S. CPI.

text.p: Swedish shares traded lower on Thursday morning ahead of U.S. consumer price data due out at 1230 GMT.
The Stockholm general index fell 0.55 percent to 3,189.43 after shares worth 1.86 billion crowns changed hands.
"This is a new situation now with people seeing that the economy in Sweden and the U.S. are strong," one broker said. "The market is worried about higher inflation and higher interest rates."
Market heavyweights Ericsson and Astra were both lower.
Ericsson was two crowns lower at 354 while drugs major Astra slipped one to 133.5.
Speciality toolmaker Sandvik rose four to 257 crowns. This move came after Handelsbanken raised its profit forecast for 1997 by 7.7 percent.
The bank sector fared the worst, losing 2.17 percent.
Nordbanken posted a 21 percent fall in operating profits in the first half of 1997 which was in line with market expectations. Its share fell four to 266 crowns.
S-E-Banken also fell four to 86 crowns after reporting a disappoiting first half earlier this week.
"The sector in general and S-E-Banken had traded up on restructuring rumours," one broker said who saw the fall partly as a correction to recent banking gains.

Forestry company MoDo was the last of Sweden's key foresters to report for the six months, posting a better than expected profit after financial items of 917 million crowns against 1.66 billion crowns a year ago.
Its share fell four crowns to 293.
